newsitem.title: USA: Fairfax County, Va., board okays $1.77 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Fairfax County, Va., board okays $1.77 bln budget.

text.p: The Fairfax County, Va., board on Monday approved a $1.77 billion budget for next year that calls for no new taxes and limited changes in government programs, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
The board voted 8-to-2, the Post reported.

The budget for fiscal 1998, which would increase spending from this year by 4.9 percent, includes $819.7 million for the school system and money to hire 13 police officers and dispatchers. The budget also restores some of the programs for the elderly and the environment that were cut last year, the Post reported. The county faced a budget crunch last year.
Under the budget, the overall government staff, excluding schools, will decline by nine positions to about 10,770.

The real estate tax rate will remain at $1.23 per $100 of assessed value, but because residential real estate values dropped slightly this year, the average residential tax bill will go down by $12, the Post reported.
